summary: Tested the locked shared layout on the backend and frontend. Backend: 14/14 pytest pass (6 new layout tests plus the existing book tests). content_hash is stable (2b02b9e336f17475). GET /api/layout/<hash>:v1 returns 230 pages with no _id. An unknown key returns 404, a wrong-hash POST returns 409, and a pages-not-list POST returns 400. Re-POSTing the same key with 1 page returns and keeps 230 pages (first write wins). Frontend in flip mode at 1920x800, 1280x720 and 390x844: the indicator shows 'Hal. 0 / 229' everywhere. All 169 .flip-page .page-body elements have scrollHeight <= clientHeight. TOC numbers match on every viewport (profil-penulis 225, bab-1 22, bab-8 92, bab-10 122). Only GET /api/layout is called on load, with no POST, so the stored layout is reused. Regression: the TOC jump to bab-8 lands on 91-92 with chapter-opener-8 visible. The continue card (ht-page=40) resumes to 39-40. Reading mode toggles both ways. Highlighting bab-1:3 sets blk-hl and stores it in ht-hl. The PDF modal says 230 pages, and the downloaded PDF has 230 pages (24.8MB).

minor.issue: No auth and little validation: only checks that pages is a list and under 8MB. The first client to post a layout for a new content hash locks it forever, even if it is a buggy or malicious client, or one whose web fonts failed to load and fell back to another font. There is no admin reset short of bumping LAYOUT_VERSION or editing the DB.

action_items: Optional hardening: before computing or saving a layout, check that the fonts actually loaded (document.fonts.check for each FONTS entry) so a fallback-font layout is never locked. Also validate pages on the server (e.g. a count range, each page has sk or type).
Optional: add a protected endpoint or script to reset db.layouts for a key.
critical_code_review_comments: layoutStore.getLockedLayout: any GET error other than 404 (network or 5xx) makes loadBook throw and shows reader-error, even though computing the layout locally would work. Consider falling back to compute() in that case.
Fit on other browsers and engines (Safari, Firefox) relies only on the 26px LAYOUT_SAFETY margin. Only Chromium was checked for overflow.
Switching flip to reading mode snaps to the section start (39-40 becomes Hal. 30, and switching back gives 29-30). This is section-level by design and was already the case before this change.
The double GET /api/layout on load comes from React.StrictMode in dev only. Harmless.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_book_api.py (section count 38 -> 40; the old test was out of date)
seed_data_creation: None. The stored layout 2b02b9e336f17475:v1 was left intact; the overwrite attempt was rejected as designed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use a new browser context with add_init_script guarded by sessionStorage to set localStorage (ht-mode, ht-page). Setting it and then reloading races with the app writing ht-page=0. PDF: click btn-download-pdf, then pdf-start-button. The download takes about 2-3 minutes in the test env. Highlight blocks are div[data-hl-id] and get the blk-hl class. TOC numbers are in [data-testid=toc-link-<key>] .toc-side-num.
